summary: A new White House policy directive has set a goal of supporting 1,000 rocket launches annually by 2030, marking a major policy push for domestic space operations. Internationally, China has abruptly postponed the launch of its uncrewed Chang'e-7 mission to the lunar south pole due to adverse weather and launch conditions. In the commercial sector, SpaceX plans to eventually retire its Falcon 9 rocket once Starship becomes fully operational, even as the company prepares for its 100th Falcon 9 flight of the year to establish a new vehicle-reuse record, while satellite startup Starcloud announced a $250 million Series A extension. On the military front, the U.S. Navy revealed a new long-range air-to-air missile designated "Malice"—a system the U.S. Air Force is closely monitoring—as General Atomics outlined plans for a new "Wildfire" drone for the Pentagon. In scientific developments, NASA deployed MAIA air sensors to begin mapping pollution in Addis Ababa, while new agency research detailed how the sun's early galactic trajectory helped shape Earth's climate. Looking ahead, observers should watch for NASA's upcoming launch of the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope from Florida as mission coverage preparations get underway.
